This is more than an entry-level role. It's an opportunity to learn how global agricultural commodities move from farm to customer, gain hands-on exposure to international markets, and develop the commercial skills needed to succeed in a fast-paced trading environment.

What Makes Commodity Trading Different?

When people hear the word "trader," they often think of hedge funds, investment banks, or trading financial instruments from behind a screen.

That's not what this role is.

We are looking for individuals who are passionate about the business of moving and merchandising physical commodities. Success in this program comes from curiosity about supply chains, market fundamentals, customer relationships, and global trade. While futures and risk management are important components of the role, this is first and foremost a career path in physical commodity trading and merchandising, not a traditional financial markets trading role.

At LDC, you'll learn how commodities are sourced, transported, stored, marketed, and sold around the world. You'll gain exposure to supply and demand dynamics, logistics, risk management, customer relationships, and commercial strategy while helping move essential products through the global food and agriculture supply chain.

Whether it's understanding crop conditions, analyzing market trends, evaluating trade flows, or supporting commercial decisions, you'll develop the skills and business acumen needed to build a long-term career in commodity trading.

What You'll Experience

As a Trader Trainee, you'll participate in LDC's Global Commercial Graduate Program and gain exposure to multiple areas of the business through structured rotations, formal training, mentorship, and real-world commercial experience. The program is designed to develop market awareness, analytical rigor, commercial acumen, adaptability, and relationship-building skills required for success in commodity trading.

Throughout the program, you'll:

• Learn how physical agricultural commodities are traded in domestic and international markets.
• Develop an understanding of market fundamentals, pricing, risk management, and trade execution.
• Analyze supply and demand trends, market research, and commercial opportunities.
• Gain exposure to logistics, execution, research, operations, and commercial teams.
• Participate in formal development courses covering trading fundamentals, market analysis, risk management, execution, and business communications.
• Receive mentorship and coaching from experienced traders and commercial leaders.
• Build a global network through LDC's international commercial organization.
• Work on meaningful projects that contribute directly to commercial decision-making.

What You'll Learn

By the end of the program, you'll develop experience in:

• Understanding the physical flow of commodities through domestic and export markets.
• Identifying market trends and commercial opportunities.
• Negotiating and managing risk.
• Using market intelligence to support trading and merchandising decisions.
• Leveraging data and analytics to drive commercial insights.
• Understanding logistics, quality, customer needs, and supply chain economics.
• Building strong relationships across customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.

Why Join LDC?

For more than 170 years, LDC has connected farmers, markets, and consumers around the world. As part of our Trader Trainee Program, you'll gain exposure to global commodity markets, work alongside experienced commercial professionals, and participate in a structured development journey designed to accelerate your growth.

Through rotations, formal learning, mentorship, and hands-on commercial experience, you'll build the foundation for a successful career in commodity trading, merchandising, marketing, research, or other commercial leadership roles. Graduates who successfully complete the program may have the opportunity to transition into permanent commercial positions within the organization.

If you're ready to launch a career at the intersection of global markets, agriculture, analytics, and commercial strategy, we encourage you to apply and join the next generation of trading talent at LDC.

Who We're Looking For

We're hiring for potential, not prior trading experience.

You may be a great fit if you are:

• Graduating with a Bachelor's or Master's degree by Summer 2027, preferably in economics, finance or mathematics.
• Passionate about global trade, agriculture, economics, supply chains, or commodity markets.
• Excited by the idea of building a career in physical commodity trading and merchandising.
• Analytical and comfortable working with large amounts of data and information.
• A strong communicator who enjoys collaborating and building relationships.
• Curious, resilient, and motivated to continuously learn.
• Able to think critically, solve problems, and make informed decisions in dynamic environments.
• Must be open to relocate to either Memphis, TN or Wilton, CT.

Preferred Areas of Study

• Agricultural Economics
• Economics
• Finance
• Mathematics
• Business
• Supply Chain Management
• Data Analytics

Equivalent degrees and experiences will also be considered.

What We Offer

We provide a dynamic and stimulating international environment, which will stretch and develop your abilities and channel your skills and expertise with outstanding career development opportunities in one of the largest and most solid private companies in the world.

- Comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental and vision care coverage, flexible spending account plans, employee assistance program, life insurance and disability coverage

- 401k with Company Match

- Family Friendly Benefits including childbirth and parental leave, fertility and family building benefits

- Paid Time Off (PTO) and Paid Holidays

- Flexible work available (not applicable to all roles)

Diversity & Inclusion

LDC is driven by a set of shared values and high ethical standards, with diversity and inclusion being part of our DNA. LDC is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a working environment that embraces and values diversity, equity and inclusion.

LDC encourages diversity, supports local communities and environmental initiatives. We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Sustainable value is at the heart of our purpose as a company.

We are passionate about creating fair and sustainable value, both for our business and for other value chain stakeholders: our people, our business partners, the communities we touch and the environment around us

jobs.title: Team Lead Electronics
jobs.description:
Lead our electronics crew to new heights. Build next-level hardware – and guide the bright minds who make it happen.

As our Team Lead Electronics Engineering, you blend technical hardware expertise with people-minded leadership.

You guide a talented team of several engineers designing, testing, and refining the electronics that power our radar systems.

Reporting to our Head of Innovation, you work closely with cross-functional areas like I&D Engineering, I&D Project Management, Procurement, and our external partners.

You make sure our hardware is top quality, our processes run smoothly, and your team gets space to grow.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Team leadership and coaching: Guide and mentor a team of engineers on their daily work and project execution

 - Technical direction and standards: Define technical direction and team standards, ensuring high quality and alignment across all designs. Lead new design projects and product improvements for electrical, optical, and thermal control. Present designs and run constructive reviews with the team

 - Resource and operational management: Allocate resources efficiently, assign project tasks, and manage work schedules

 - PCB design and layout: Hands-on PCB layout creation using Altium Designer. Guide choices on RF and analog circuits, digital design, and high-speed interfaces

 - Circuit testing and verification: Oversee detailed testing, simulation, and design verification. Ensure findings are documented properly before releasing components or sub-assembly solutions to production

 - Design documentation and compliance: Keep design files, test reports, and technical specs structured and up to date. Maintain compliance with relevant IPC standards, EMC regulations, and internal procedures

 - Process improvement and partner alignment: Identify areas for operational improvement, evaluate proposed design changes to balance added value against resource expenditure, and manage contractor POs/timesheets. Collaborate directly with component suppliers, EMS partners, and academic institutions


REQUIREMENTS

 - BSc or MSc degree in Electronic Engineering or a related technical field

 - 8+ years of hands-on PCB hardware design experience with strong overall electronic design skills

 - Proven experience leading, mentoring, or coaching technical team members

 - Deep technical knowledge of RF circuits, FPGAs, high-speed interfaces, and digital design

 - Strong experience with EMC regulations and IPC standards

 - Hands-on expertise with Altium Designer and measurement equipment like VNAs and oscilloscopes

 - Basic proficiency in electromagnetic (EM) knowledge is considered a distinct asset

 - Strong attention to detail, proactive mindset, and ability to balance leadership with hands-on technical work

 - Fluent in English, both written and spoken, with great cross-cultural communication skills

 - Willingness to travel occasionally to project or partner sites



N.B. Don't worry if you don't tick every box. Our mission is a journey, and there's plenty to learn along the way. If most of this fits, we'd love to hear from you.

A Certificate of Conduct (VOG) and a background check are part of our screening process. We appreciate your understanding.


WHAT'S IN FOR YOU

 - Working for a Great Place to Work® certified company

 - Comprehensive pension plan

 - Commuting allowance

 - 30 days of paid holiday leave (with the possibility to buy 3 additional days)

 - Opportunities to develop your skills even further through training and certifications

 - High quality laptop/desktop, monitor, headphones, and any other equipment necessary for your role

 - An international team of 30+ nationalities, full of high performance colleagues you can exchange experiences with and learn from. As well as having a lot of fun in our social events and Friday drinks

Robin Radar is a technology leader in tracking and classifying small objects. Our radars and software help prevent bird strikes in aviation, reduce the impact of wind farms on wildlife, and protect critical infrastructure from drone threats. Our work shows up at airports, wind farms, military sites and nature reserves around the world.

We're one of the top 10 fastest-growing companies in the Netherlands, with a crew of bright minds across 30+ nationalities. Growth doesn't mean we lose the plot – eyes on the skies, feet on the ground. Our values keep us grounded: WE TRUST. WE OWN IT. WE AIM HIGH.

Want to work on next-level radar tech, solve real problems, and never have to pretend your job has meaning? You'll fit right in – we're saving you a seat.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Originator
jobs.description:
Rothesay is the UK’s largest pensions insurance specialist, purpose-built to protect pension schemes and their members’ pensions. With over £74 billion of assets under management, we secure the pensions of nearly one million people and pay out, on average, approximately £355 million in pension payments each month.

Rothesay is dedicated to providing excellence in customer service alongside prudent underwriting, a conservative investment strategy and the careful management of risk. We are trusted by the pension schemes of some of the UK’s best known companies to provide pension solutions, including British Airways, Cadbury’s, the Civil Aviation Authority, the Co-Operative Group, National Grid, NatWest, Morrisons and Telent.

Rothesay Asset Management North America (“RAM-NA”) is headquartered in NYC and focuses on sourcing long-dated fixed income assets in North America. Since being established in 2018, it has originated over $12.5bn of high-quality investments for the UK balance sheet.

At Rothesay, we are striving to transform our industry. We believe deeply in creating real security for the future and our leadership in finding new and better ways to do that is the key to our success. To do that, we need the very brightest original thinkers to bring creativity as well as rigor. Rothesay is a rewarding place to work, where quality people can thrive and prosper. We pride ourselves on the connections our people build, many of whom have been with us for over ten years.

In general, we are looking for a smart, commercial individual with an excellent academic record, strong quantitative and problem-solving abilities and a high degree of adaptability, with a genuine intellectual appetite to expand their existing skillset.

Job title:                           Infrastructure Originator

Reports to:                       Head of Infrastructure RAM-NA

Location:                          New York, NY

Type of position:              Permanent

RESPONSIBILITIES

Deal Origination & Evaluation

• Contribute to the sourcing of infrastructure debt opportunities in North America by leveraging Rothesay’s and own relationship networks in the infrastructure market, including sponsors, advisors, banks, broker dealers, asset managers and consultants.

• Support such networks by promoting Rothesay’s profile in industry gatherings and conferences with relevant external counterparties and market participants

• Conduct detailed due diligence, credit analysis and underwriting of infrastructure lending opportunities including identification and assessment of risks, market underwriting and scenario analysis

• Promote a culture of collaboration among the different teams within Rothesay to foster robust relative value discussions to generate optimal risk-adjusted returns for the overall portfolio

• Contribute to the preparation of complex dynamic financial models to analyze investment opportunities, test assumptions and run sensitivities

• Analyze and contribute to the definition of debt structures and covenant packages appropriate for every transaction, with appropriate pricing supported by relative value analysis

Deal Execution & Ongoing Management

• Manage all aspects of the execution of infrastructure transactions, including underwriting, due diligence, structuring, management of the investment committee process, legal documentation, and asset management

• Review and provide input to any commercial aspects of the transaction agreement. Work with counsel to ensure that the transaction documents reflect commercially agreed position

• Review due diligence materials and robustly challenge assumptions and conclusions to ensure that the due diligence process has been thoroughly completed and potential risks identified

• Coordinate the preparation and the presentation to the appropriate committee of detailed investment committee papers, which concisely present the opportunity, clearly identify and assess the risks of the deal and any other material due diligence findings, and present appropriate external and internal metrics for consideration

• Demonstrate strong commercial judgment and project management skills for the management of internal parties involved in the deal execution process, as well as 3rd party advisors and borrowers

• Contribute to the ongoing oversight of portfolio investments originated, including participating in the definition of the strategy and negotiations related to amendments, waivers, restructurings, and other credit events with transactions in the portfolio

QUALIFICATIONS

Experience

• Bachelor’s or equivalent degree from a leading university in a relevant highly quantitative degree such as mathematics, economics, finance, or related scientific area.

• 5+ years of experience in infrastructure banking or investment, including sourcing, structuring, execution, and management of complex transactions, with a demonstrated track record of sourcing and executing infrastructure debt investments in North America

• Established relationships with relevant infrastructure sponsors, advisors, banks, broker dealers, asset managers and consultants.

• Experience with investment-grade and below investment-grade lending, preferably both in bank loan and bond/note formats, including advanced modeling and due diligence skills

• Strong credit judgment, financial analysis skills, and ability to balance risk and return. Experience in debt or hard assets with non-performing loans/workout experience to be valued additionally

Competencies

• Technical skills - Strong technical and analytical skills, including a very strong hands-on grasp of MS Excel, with a particular focus on cashflow modeling, risk analysis and creative problem solving. Attention to detail, and initiative to continually broaden their knowledge

• Drive and motivation – A self-starter, with the ability to successfully handle multiple tasks, taking initiative to improve their own performance, working intensely under time pressure towards challenging goals and persisting in the face of obstacles or setbacks

• Commercial awareness – Ability to see the big picture alongside the quantitative analysis, with an effective and pragmatic analysis of complex issues

• Judgment and problem solving - Thinking ahead to identify clear objectives, with anticipation of questions, planning for contingencies, and seeking alternative solutions

• Teamwork – Evidence of being a strong team player, who collaborates with others within and across teams, encourages other team members to participate and contribute and acknowledges others' contributions

• Communication skills – Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to present complex investment views clearly and collaborate effectively across the organization

• Creativity and innovation – Willingness to look for new ways to improve current approaches and develop creative solutions that are grounded in reality and have practical value

• Influence over outcomes – Ability to present sound, persuasive rationale for ideas and recommendations, engaging with others in collaborative discussion seeking maximization of value for the organization

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Deposition & Etch Equipment and Production Engineer (H/F)
jobs.description:
Alice & Bob is developing the first universal, fault-tolerant quantum computer to solve the world’s hardest problems.
The quantum computer we envision building is based on a new kind of superconducting qubit: the Schrödinger cat qubit 🐈‍⬛. In comparison to other superconducting platforms, cat qubits have the astonishing ability to implement quantum error correction autonomously!
 
We're a diverse team of 250+ brilliant minds from over 35 countries united by a single goal: to revolutionise computing with a practical fault-tolerant quantum machine. Are you ready to take on unprecedented challenges and contribute to revolutionising technology? Join us, and let's shape the future of quantum computing together!


The role
We've just built a cleanroom in Aubervilliers dedicated to the fabrication of superconducting quantum devices — a step change in our wafer capacity and in how fast we can iterate on qubit designs. The Cleanroom Operations team, created now, owns the throughput of that line.
You join as a Tool Owner and hands-on production engineer on the deposition and etch scope: superconductor deposition, metal evaporation including shadow-angle evaporation, and dry etching. These are the long-run tools the weekly output depends on — when a chamber goes down, the line feels it within a day.
You're accountable for a defined set of tools: their uptime, their maintenance, their utilization, and the qualified recipes that run on them at industrial cadence. For each tool you form a binome with a Process Owner from Process Development Engineering — you own the asset and its execution, they own the recipe and its process window, and you solve the hard problems and qualify operators together. Recipe ownership and process innovation sit with them; making the tool deliver, reliably and at cadence, is yours.
You're joining a team at its creation, reporting to the Cleanroom Operations Manager. You'll build the operation rather than inherit one.
We're hiring two Tool Owners for this team, one on lithography and one on deposition and etching. If your experience spans both, apply to whichever fits best — we'll route you.

White Pine Innovations is seeking a Part-Time Security Cooperation (SC) Instructor to support the Defense Security Cooperation University (DSCU): Contractor shall provide qualified support to the research-based mission and training programs. The core focus of this support shall be research, analysis, and teaching. Significant experience with and knowledge of the US government Security Cooperation program is highly preferred.

This position is part-time at approximately 10 hours per week.

Roles and Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Conduct research and providing analytical support to DSCU faculty and staff.

• Lead and establish priorities for the vetting of content, product development, reviews, dissemination strategy, and coordination of stakeholders.

• Engage with DSCU stakeholders to incorporate case studies, lessons learned, and contemporary issues into instructional content.

• Coordinate instructional content and updates with DSCU academic leadership and program staff to ensure consistency and compliance with accreditation requirements.

Basic Requirements:

• Master’s degree in a related SC field.

jobs.title: Claims Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT 8FLEET

8Fleet is a Los Angeles–based technology and logistics company building the operational infrastructure behind modern rideshare fleets. We operate in Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Atlanta and Miami, with more markets launching soon.


ABOUT THE ROLE

At 8Fleet, claims sit at the intersection of fleet availability, driver experience, insurance costs, repair expenses, operational risk and company economics. Today our accident and vehicle-incident claims run largely on manual workflows in Google Sheets. You'll manage those claims directly while building the claims function from the ground up: the processes, the standards and the reporting that turn claims data into decisions that save money.

This role sits on our Central Operations team and is based in Los Angeles or San Francisco.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own accident and vehicle-incident claims across all markets, from first notice of loss through investigation, repair coordination, negotiation, settlement and closure.

 - Build the incident intake and triage process, including what happens in the first 24 hours.

 - Be the main contact for carriers, TPAs, adjusters and defense counsel, and hold them to clear expectations.

 - Run subrogation and recovery as a real workstream.

 - Partner with market leaders to turn accident trends and risk patterns into operational changes.

 - Build claims reporting leadership can plan against: frequency, severity, cost per vehicle and open-claim aging.

 - Move claims onto a proper system and support insurance renewals with clean loss data.

 - Keep us compliant with state requirements in CA, GA, FL and each new market.

 - Build the team as volume grows.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 7+ years in auto, fleet, transportation or commercial auto claims, including owning a claims function or program end to end.

 - Experience with third-party liability and bodily injury claims.

 - Strong claim-file judgment and experience working with TPAs and defense counsel.

 - Confidence pushing back on carriers on reserves and coverage.

 - Multi-state experience, ideally including California.

 - A methodical approach and comfort building process where none exists.


NICE TO HAVE

 - AIC, SCLA, ARM or similar designation.

 - Self-insured or large-deductible program experience.

 - Fleet, rideshare, delivery or logistics background.

 - People-management experience.


COMPENSATION

Base Salary: $130,000–$150,000 + equity


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Us:

Quartermaster is building the world's most comprehensive maritime intelligence platform. Our SmartMast™ system transforms commercial and civilian vessels into a persistent, distributed sensing network—combining HD video, AI, radar, RF sensing, and AIS to deliver real-time maritime domain awareness at global scale. With 600+ sensors deployed across 25+ countries and more than 400,000 vessels identified outside of AIS, we are setting a new standard for what ocean surveillance and safety can look like. We are a mission-driven, high-velocity team building dual-use technology for defense agencies, coast guards, and commercial maritime operators.


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Quartermaster is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Technical Program Manager (TPM) to drive execution across complex, multi-disciplinary engineering programs. In this role, you will coordinate efforts across hardware, software, manufacturing, and operations teams to ensure our ruggedized sensing systems are delivered on time, on spec, and ready for deployment. You’ll serve as the connective tissue between technical contributors and strategic milestones—tracking progress, identifying risks, and enabling decision-making at all levels. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments and has a passion for aligning technical work with real-world outcomes.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own end-to-end planning and execution of major product development programs, from concept through production and deployment.

 - Define program schedules, milestones, and critical paths across hardware, software, and manufacturing tracks.

 - Facilitate cross-functional collaboration by running standups, sprint planning, and milestone reviews with engineering and ops teams.

 - Identify dependencies, resource needs, and execution risks—proactively escalating and driving resolution.

 - Maintain clear, up-to-date program documentation including Gantt charts, issue trackers, and progress dashboards.

 - Support new product introduction (NPI) and field rollout planning, ensuring readiness across supply chain, QA, and logistics.

 - Act as primary point of contact for internal stakeholders on program status, scope, and decision timelines.

 - Coordinate change management, ensuring that scope or requirement shifts are clearly communicated and integrated across teams.

 - Contribute to continuous improvement of program processes, tooling, and collaboration practices.

 - Help ensure programs align with company OKRs and strategic priorities.

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Enigneer
jobs.description:
About Us:

Quartermaster is building the world's most comprehensive maritime intelligence platform. Our SmartMast™ system transforms commercial and civilian vessels into a persistent, distributed sensing network—combining HD video, AI, radar, RF sensing, and AIS to deliver real-time maritime domain awareness at global scale. With 600+ sensors deployed across 25+ countries and more than 400,000 vessels identified outside of AIS, we are setting a new standard for what ocean surveillance and safety can look like. We are a mission-driven, high-velocity team building dual-use technology for defense agencies, coast guards, and commercial maritime operators.


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We are seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer to design and release hardware for Quartermaster’s Smartmast systems and related marine products. This role focuses on marine electromechanical hardware for harsh outdoor environments, especially enclosures, mounting systems, cable integration, and production-ready design.

The right candidate has strong experience with marine electronics or comparable outdoor electromechanical systems and can work effectively on short R&D timelines while delivering hardware that is reliable, manufacturable, and ready to scale. This role is primarily remote and includes occasional travel to vessel locations or manufacturing sites.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Design and release mechanical hardware, including enclosures, mounts, brackets, interfaces, and installation solutions.

 - Design for sealing, corrosion resistance, vibration, serviceability, manufacturability, and assembly quality.

 - Own mechanical portions of projects from concept through prototyping, testing, and production release.

 - Work with electrical, operations, manufacturing, and suppliers to resolve integration issues and improve reliability.

 - Define and improve standards for cabling, connectorization, mounting, and field installation.


QUALIFICATIONS (PREFERRED):

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 5+ years of experience designing mechanical hardware for marine electronics, outdoor electronics, or electromechanical systems in harsh environments.

 - Strong CAD proficiency, preferably in Onshape, with the ability to create production-ready parts and assemblies.

 - Experience designing for manufacturing, assembly, reliability, and field service.

 - Working knowledge of electromechanical integration, including enclosures, cable routing, connectors, and hardware interfaces.

 - Ability to work independently and communicate clearly with remote teams, vendors, and manufacturing partners.

 - Industrial design experience is a plus.


WORK ENVIRONMENT:

 - Flexible working hours, with occasional intensive sprints.

 - Occasional travel to vessel installations or manufacturing sites.

 - Opportunity to work on innovative projects with a global impact.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Lead Architect/Engineer, Front End
jobs.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry Media is transforming how medical and healthcare marketers engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and consumers through data, technology, and omnichannel innovation. Real Chemistry Media's product and technology teams sit at the heart of this meaningful work by building tools that increase impact. In support of our mission to help life-changing medicines and therapies reach their full market potential, we are building an enterprise platform for omnichannel orchestration in healthcare marketing.

Our technology enables healthcare organizations to design, deploy, and optimize HCP journeys through a scalable, self-service product that connects to their existing marketing and data systems. The platform is live with early users and on track with rapid growth milestones, so the decisions made over the next year will be influential in shaping the product's future.

We are hiring a Lead Engineer, Front End to lead the architecture and hands-on delivery of the interfaces our customers use to build and manage HCP journeys. You will lead front-end engineering, hire and grow the team behind it, and partner closely with the back end lead and product designer so the platform's interface, data model, and design system evolve together. The team is small and we're building a lot, so there are a lot of opportunities for ownership and influence.

What You'll Do:

• Lead front-end architecture and hands-on delivery for the platform's user-facing product, from early prototypes through production.

• Lead the journey-builder canvas — a direct-manipulation, graph-based interface — as it scales to more complex journeys and larger data volumes.

• Define API contracts together with the back end lead, so the interface and the data model evolve as one system.

• Drive the code side of the design system and the design-to-code workflow, in partnership with the product designer, who leads the design system itself.

• Direct how AI-driven guardrails and model behavior are rendered and made trustworthy in the product.

• Hire and lead a front-end engineering team as it grows, setting a high bar for code quality and CI-enforced testing.

• Support and set standards for agentic coding on your team, backed by real company investment in the tools, not just tolerance for their use.

• Partner with product and design on problem definition, scope, and sequencing from the start of each effort.

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

• You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.

• You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.

• You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

What You Should Have:

• 8+ years in front-end or full-stack engineering, including 2+ years leading a team.

• Experience leading front-end architecture for a B2B or enterprise product, ideally one with a complex, data-dense, or direct-manipulation UI (a canvas, graph editor, or similar).

• Track record hiring and growing engineers, and running a technical interview loop from scratch.

• Comfortable directing and reviewing agentic or AI-assisted coding, with the judgment to know what to hold to human review regardless of how the code was produced.

• Fluency defining and maintaining API contracts across a team boundary.

• Ability to turn ambiguous product problems into a sequenced, shippable technical plan.

• Comfort with ambiguity and a fast-moving, still-small engineering org.

• Bonus points for pharma or HCP marketing experience — or any complex, regulated marketing data environment (ad tech, financial services marketing, health systems).

Pay Range: $175,000-$200,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

jobs.title: Integrated Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About Norm Ai
Norm Ai, the agentic law company, has a client base with a combined $30 trillion in assets under management.


Norm Ai pioneered Legal Engineering, the process that empowers lawyers to build and supervise domain-specific AI agents with Norm’s proprietary suite of no-code software tools. Norm Ai technology is deployed inside many of the largest and most consequential institutions in the world.


Norm Ai is also the technology behind Norm Law, LLP, a separate but affiliated AI-native law firm built for the era of agentic AI. Norm Law’s attorneys advise leading institutions across private funds, private equity, venture capital, real estate, registered funds, and financial regulation, using the same legal intelligence platform that powers Norm Ai’s products.

AI Fluency:
Norm Ai expects all team members to be fluent in AI. Successful candidates actively use AI in their day-to-day work to support thinking, creation, and problem-solving. They use it to improve the quality and speed of their work and to continuously refine how work gets done end-to-end.

Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate and discuss their AI usage throughout the interview process, including concrete examples of tools, workflows, and outcomes. We look for practical, hands-on experience, not theoretical familiarity.



This Role

Norm is looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to design, orchestrate, scale, and measure integrated marketing campaigns that support our business priorities and drive demand, engagement, and revenue with our target clients. As a key member of our marketing team, you'll build the campaign frameworks and cross-channel motions that connect our content, events, digital programs, and account-based efforts into cohesive journeys that move buyers from awareness to activation.

This role requires a sophisticated understanding of marketing with demonstrated success in integrated campaign strategy and execution across the full customer lifecycle. You'll develop and execute comprehensive campaign strategies and create compelling programs that bring to life our brand narrative and company mission.



What You’ll Do

 - Coordinate campaigns: Design and lead integrated campaigns across key audiences and target clients, establishing scalable frameworks and processes that connect digital, events, content, and ABM channels into cohesive buyer journeys

 - Execute the strategy: Create and implement campaign programs including thought leadership moments, paid programming, nurture streams, executive engagement programs, and ABM activations.

 - Drive cross-functional collaboration: Collaborate with stakeholders across Marketing, GTM, and Norm Law to ensure campaigns align with company-wide strategy while meeting client- and narrative-specific needs

 - Maintain the message: Coordinate across Marketing to ensure consistent messaging and positioning across all campaign touchpoints

 - Drive project management: Manage campaign resources including agency partners, vendors, and internal creative and content stakeholders to deliver programs on time and on budget

 - Own the metrics: Drive continuous improvement through post-campaign analysis, stakeholder feedback, and data-driven optimization



What We’re Looking For

Core Qualifications

 - 3-5+ years of experience in demand generation, integrated marketing, or campaigns.

 - Have a track record of successfully building and scaling integrated campaign programs that span digital, events, content, and ABM channels

 - Have strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to campaign optimization and attribution

 - Have strong project management skills with experience managing complex, multi-channel campaigns simultaneously

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity and thrive in fast-paced, evolving environments with a bias for thoughtful action

 - Creative and strategic thinking, you can turn a vague idea or goal into a concrete, compelling plan and see it through to execution



Nice to Have

 - Familiarity with AI, legal technology, regulation and policy, or another complex enterprise category

 - Scaled integrated marketing programs across channels

 - Expertise in 2-3 marketing channels (paid, webinars, content, etc.) with a passion to excel in new ones (AEO, social, etc.)



What Success Looks Like

30 Days

 - Develop a strong understanding of Norm’s GTM model, business priorities, audiences, and existing campaign commitments.

 - Build relationships with key internal stakeholders and assess current partners, processes, and capabilities.

60 Days

 - Present a prioritized integrated campaign plan, including what channels to invest in, areas for optimization, and what to deprioritize

 - Define initial concepts, target audiences, channel tactics, budgets, and success measures for priority programs.

90 Days

 - Establish a clear roadmap for Norm’s integrated campaigns

 - Move the first priority program into execution with aligned stakeholders, ownership, timelines, and measurement.



Compensation and Benefits

Range:  $120K - $160K

The range displayed in this job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new-hire salary for this position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Equity: Included

Benefits: 401(k) with employer match; health, dental, and vision coverage; unlimited paid time off; free lunch in the office daily; and an employee referral bonus program.

Relocation: [If applicable] Financial support to ease your move to New York City, designed to make the transition smooth and stress-free.



Work Location:

Location: New York City

Work model: Hybrid

In-office expectation: 3-4 days per week

Travel expectation: Occasional (30%) travel for events, conferences, partnerships, and on-site production.



To learn more about Norm Ai, visit our website https://www.norm.ai.

Lead Finance Partner: Product FP&A

US - Remote

Role Summary

Our mission at HubSpot is to help millions of organizations grow better. As a Product FP&A Lead Finance Partner, you'll own the financial strategy and forecasting for HubSpot's triple-digit-$M platform cost base, partnering with Engineering, Infrastructure, and Procurement to turn complex cloud and AI economics into clear business decisions. This is an individual contributor role on a lean team with regular, direct exposure to senior Finance leadership. This role blends core FP&A ownership with high-impact strategic projects: you'll run the platform COGS process while leading work across compute demand planning, 9-figure annualized vendor renewals, and feature-level cost attribution in one of the fastest-evolving cost structures in the business. High autonomy, high visibility, and real influence over how HubSpot thinks about AI infrastructure cost.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead Platform COGS planning, forecasting, and business partnership with Eng and TPM as the Finance DRI — driving forecast accuracy and leadership-ready cost insights through recurring business reviews, with process automation where it adds leverage.

• Lead financial modeling and scenario analysis for HubSpot's hyperscaler contract renewal, partnering with Engineering, Infrastructure, Procurement, and Finance leadership to shape contract strategy and monitor commitments.

• Build durable, driver-based forecasting frameworks for LLM/compute demand and platform spend, translating technical metrics — compute, storage, networking, model usage — into workload-level forecasts that scale with HubSpot's AI infrastructure needs.

• Partner with Engineering and Data teams to connect platform usage and infrastructure architecture to feature-level cost attribution and gross-margin analysis, informing pricing, packaging, and architecture decisions.

• Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives from ambiguous questions to decision-ready recommendations, setting the pace and keeping stakeholders aligned.

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in FP&A, strategic finance, infrastructure finance, FinOps, or similar, involving complex cost structures and cross-functional decision-making.

• Solid understanding of COGS, gross margin, and unit economics in a cloud, SaaS, or usage-driven environment, including how cost structures, architecture, and commercial commitments shape them.

• Experience building driver-based models, forecasts, and scenario/sensitivity analyses with imperfect or evolving data.

• Demonstrated ownership of ambiguous, multi-stakeholder projects end-to-end — from analysis through recommendation and execution — with judgment on when to go deep vs. 80/20.

• Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders in Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Procurement, and/or Strategy & Operations by building credibility and translating complex cloud/AI economics clearly, balancing rigor with speed.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience at a high-growth, multi-product SaaS, cloud infrastructure, or AI business.

• Experience working with large or complex datasets, with demonstrated ability to navigate SQL workflows, AI tools, or other analytical tools to identify meaningful insights.

• Experience with AWS economics, including Compute Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, commitment attainment, or large cloud vendor renewals.

• Experience developing product-, feature-, or workload-level cost attribution and unit-economic frameworks.

Hellbender Inc. is a Pennsylvania Benefit Corporation who partners with innovators to mature their Artificial Intelligence enabled computing sensors and produce their solutions onshore at prototype to high volumes.

Hellbender is intentionally forming an inclusive work environment and is committed to uplifting the historically marginalized identities including veterans, women, transgender people and underrepresented races in our community and industry.

Job Summary

The Senior Technical Program Manager (STPM) leads cross-functional programs that bring Hellbender's hardware and software products from concept through production launch. This role coordinates engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and program stakeholders to ensure technical programs are delivered on schedule, within budget, and to specification. The STPM serves as the central point of accountability for program timelines, risk management, and cross-team communication in a multi-shift technology manufacturing environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Plan, schedule, and drive execution of complex, cross-functional technical programs from requirements definition through design, prototyping, testing, and production release

• Serve as the primary liaison between engineering, manufacturing/production, quality assurance, supply chain, and program stakeholders, ensuring alignment on scope, schedule, and deliverables

• Develop and maintain integrated program schedules, risk registers, and dependency maps; proactively identify and resolve schedule conflicts and resource constraints

• Facilitate program reviews, design reviews, and milestone gate meetings; prepare and present status updates to engineering leadership and executive stakeholders

• Coordinate with Purchasing and Supply Chain to manage long-lead components, vendor deliverables, and program budgets, including tracking program-level costs against forecast

• Partner with Quality to ensure programs meet applicable engineering, safety, and regulatory requirements, including any customer- or contract-specific technical specifications

• Identify, document, and mitigate program risks, including technical risks, resource constraints, and supplier or schedule dependencies; escalate issues appropriately

• Support new product introduction (NPI) activities, coordinating transition of programs from engineering development into multi-shift production

• Maintain program documentation, including requirements traceability, change logs, and post-program lessons-learned reviews

• Coordinate with Compliance/Facility Security to ensure program activities, documentation, and access controls comply with applicable export control (ITAR) and government contracting requirements for programs involving controlled technical data

• Other duties as assigned

Qualifications, Skills, and Attributes

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Program/Project Management, or a related technical field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

• 10 – 15 years of experience managing technical or engineering programs, preferably in a hardware, electronics, or technology manufacturing environment

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent programs and cross-functional teams without direct authority

• Strong working knowledge of program/project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Stage-Gate, waterfall) and tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira)

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to senior leadership

Hellbender is a growing business and follows a policy that prioritizes internal promotions. As new positions are created, new opportunities for advancement will be created as well.

jobs.title: Research Scientist II
jobs.description:
About our Company:

Universal DX, Inc. is an international Company with a highly experienced team focused on cracking cancer’s code. Through our multi-omics and bioinformatics models, we have figured out how to read the disease’s signals in blood with high accuracy to detect cancer in its earliest stages. Starting with a colorectal cancer screening liquid biopsy test, we are building a multi-cancer platform that can identify the unique DNA regions associated with different types of cancers.

The Opportunity:

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist II specializing in Reagent QC Development to join our rapidly growing team. This role will play a critical role in developing and executing quality control (QC) methods for reagents used in our NGS-based diagnostic assays. Reporting to the Director, Reagent Development, this role will oversee reagent QC method development as well as establish reagent freeze/thaw (F/T) stability and onboard reagent stability to ensure robust assay performance and compliance with regulatory standards.  This role will also play an integral role in coordinating the transfer of reagent QC methods and related documentation to the Reagent Manufacturing team.

You will be part of a team that is passionate about developing novel diagnostic tests for the early detection of cancer. As part of the team, you will be in a Company that aims to have a huge positive impact on society by achieving the ambitious purpose of “making cancer a curable disease by detecting it earlier”

How You’ll Contribute:

Reagent QC Method Development:

• Support the development and validation of system-level QC methods for assay-critical reagents used in next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based in vitro diagnostic (IVD) assays, ensuring accuracy, reliability, and compliance with CLSI guidelines and regulatory standards.

• Design and implement studies to support a comprehensive validation framework for reagent QC methods.

• Optimize and scale QC workflows to enhance efficiency, reproducibility, and robustness, integrating risk-based approaches to reagent quality control.

Reagent Stability Studies:

• Design and execute studies to establish the in use and long-term stability of reagents, ensuring long-term reliability.

• Conduct onboard stability studies to evaluate reagent performance under simulated real-world conditions.

• Partner with Data science team to analyze stability data and determine reagent shelf life and usage guidelines.

Documentation and Reporting:

• Draft and review study protocols, validation reports, and other technical documentation.

• Ensure thorough and accurate record-keeping to support regulatory submissions and audits.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

• Partner with internal teams, including Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, and Regulatory Affairs, to ensure seamless integration of reagent QC strategies across the product lifecycle

• Collaborate with internal and external partners to facilitate process transfer and QC testing.

Process Optimization and Compliance:

• Identify opportunities for process improvement and implement solutions to enhance efficiency and reproducibility.

• Maintain adherence to quality management systems (QMS) and regulatory compliance throughout all QC activities.

Qualifications:

Required:

• Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Genetics, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in development reagent QC methods for NGS-based IVD assays.

• Understanding of reagent QC method development, including functional and stability testing.

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, IVDR) and industry standards (e.g., CLSI guidelines).

• Proven ability to design and manage validation studies.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.

• Comfortable working in fast-paced environment with ability to adapt to shifting priorities.

Preferred:

• Experience in oncology diagnostics or liquid biopsy assays.

• Familiarity with automation systems and high-throughput platforms.

• Prior experience transferring reagent QC methods from R&D to Manufacturing teams.

What we'll offer:

• 22 days of PTO with the possibility to carry over 10 days to the following year.

• Company Holidays, plus your Birthday off!

• Company-sponsored benefit plans, including medical, dental, and vision insurance plus life, STD, and LTD coverage, and 401(k).

• Flexible work schedule

• And more to come!

Why Now?

This is an exciting time to be at Universal DX. We are growing rapidly and starting our US operations by building up our team, starting our lab and business operations, and establishing strategic partnerships.

We are looking for passionate changemakers to be a part of our journey in this expansive time for us.

jobs.title: Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Calm

Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier. Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices. Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health, offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes. Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter. Learn more at calm.com.

What You'll Do

As a Growth Product Manager on Calm's direct-to-consumer business, you'll help more people discover, adopt, and build daily habits with Calm. You'll own the growth product strategy and roadmap, accountable for driving subscriber growth, activation, revenue per user, and retention. You'll set the priorities, design and run the experiments that test them, and partner with engineering, product design, marketing, data, and research to ship what works. Your goal is to make it effortless for users to form a lasting mindfulness habit while helping Calm reach and sustain its growth goals.

As a Product Manager working on Calm’s direct-to-consumer business, you will drive measurable impact across top-of-funnel conversion, trial-to-paid transitions, user activation, and long-term retention. You will design, execute, and analyze product experiments in collaboration with engineering, design, marketing, and data science teams.

Day to day, you will:

• Own growth strategy and roadmap: Develop and own Calm's growth product strategy and roadmap, translating company revenue, subscriber, and DAU goals into a prioritized set of bets across activation, conversion, and retention.

• Run a high-velocity experiment program: Form sharp hypotheses, design and ship A/B tests with engineering and data science, and read results honestly — including the ones that don't win.

• Remove friction from key journeys: Use quantitative and qualitative data to find where users drop off in onboarding, habit-building, and account flows, then test simpler paths through them.

• Ship habit mechanics: Build the features that help users plan, track, and celebrate progress, so a first session becomes a daily practice.

• Write PRDs that make decisions easy: Spell out the job to be done, the opportunity, success metrics, and the plan to ship and iterate — then bring engineers, designers, marketers, and leadership along as the plan changes.

Who You Are

• A growth PM, or equivalent, who's owned the number: 4+ years in consumer product, with a track record of owning a growth metric (subscriber growth, conversion, retention) and setting the strategy to move it, across consumer mobile (iOS and Android) and web.

• A subscription-business operator: Fluent in the economics of consumer subscription (trial and paywall conversion, LTV, churn) and how product decisions show up in them.

• A rapid experimenter: Experienced in fast experiment design and analysis (A/B tests, holdouts, sequential testing), with the statistical judgment to know when a result is real and when it's noise.

• Data-fluent: Adept at sourcing quantitative and qualitative data to prioritize a roadmap and make feature calls, and decisive when the data won't settle it.

• A student of habit formation: You know what drives repeat daily usage and how to build the mechanics (streaks, reminders, progress, celebration) that turn a new user into a daily one.

• AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in leveraging AI tools to drive team velocity and build lasting workflows, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

• Technically agile: Comfortable discussing complexity and tradeoffs with engineers, and able to prototype your own ideas rather than wait in a queue.

• Exceptional at documentation and organization: You keep the experiment log, results archive, and roadmap docs in a state where anyone can find what was tested, what it showed, and what's live (so the team builds on its own learnings instead of rediscovering them.)

• A low-ego, persuasive partner: You present your thinking clearly in writing and in the room, to stakeholders and senior leadership alike, hold positions with conviction and update them on evidence, and make Product Design, User Acquisition, Research, and Engineering better for working with you.

Nice to Haves

• Experience in subscription-based consumer tech (onboarding, paywalls, or retention initiatives).

• Familiarity with product analytics or experimentation tools (e.g., Amplitude).

• Experience working with or passion for the health & wellness domain.

• Experience in developing features that drive habit formation and lifestyle change.

Minimum Requirements

• 4+ years of relevant experience in growth, product management, or equivalent.

Calm uses a geographic pay model that determines salaries based on the location where an employee lives. For this position, the base pay ranges across Calm’s pay tiers is as follows: $147,800 - $226,700. The base pay range represents the low and high end of Calm’s salary range for this position. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. Exact salary will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, experience and other qualifications. Calm uses employee zip code to determine which pay range applies. This role is also eligible for equity + comprehensive benefits + 401k + flexible time off.

Calm may incorporate artificial intelligence technology to support the application review process, but rest assured that human reviewers are involved in all stages of the hiring process.

Calm is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, including disabled veterans. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application or interview process, please contact Calm’s Recruiting team at recruitingaccommodations@calm.com. All accommodation requests will be handled confidentially and assessed on a case-by-case basis.

We believe that mental health is health, and every person should be considered in the discussion. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

jobs.title: Analytics Program Lead
jobs.description:
On this journey for over 12 years, Qventus is leading the transformation of healthcare. We enable hospitals to focus on what matters most: patient care. Our innovative solutions harness the power of machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to deliver exceptional outcomes and empower care teams to anticipate and resolve issues before they arise.

Our success in rapid scale across the globe is backed by some of the world's leading investors. At Qventus, you will have the opportunity to work with an exceptional, mission-driven team across the globe, and the ability to directly impact the lives of patients. We’re inspired to work with healthcare leaders on our founding vision and unlock world-class medicine through world-class operations. #LI-MB1

About the role:

We're looking for a Senior / Staff Analytics Program Lead to own the analytics product program across our global Analytics organization. While our solution analytics leads own the definitions and insights for a single solution, this role owns the analytics product function as a system: how analytics products get built, how they hold together across solutions, and how fast we can ship the next one. You are accountable for the coherence, quality, and velocity of everything the analytics function delivers, internal and external, and for steering the function toward more self-serve and agentic analytics, where trusted metric definitions let customers, internal teams, and AI agents answer more questions without an analyst in the loop.

This is a hybrid role. Most of your time goes to running the program: enforcing and evolving the analytics standards and ways of working that let each pod ship correctly, scoping and sequencing work across solutions, and partnering with platform, data/BI engineering, and context architecture to shape the technical & semantic foundations our analytics products are built on, especially as we scale towards enabling increased self-service with AI tools. The rest is hands-on. You will jump into a domain as an individual contributor when the hardest problems need you, both to unblock the team and to stay closely aligned the work you're setting the bar for. If you are energized by taking a pattern you know works and re-establishing it at a broader scale, this is that role.

Key Responsibilities:

At Qventus, Analytics is treated as a first-class product, rather than a secondary output. As the Analytics Program Lead, you will:

• Own delivery of coherent, high-quality, on-time analytics products across solutions, and hold the bar for products that are stable, maintainable, and easy to iterate and enhance over time

• Increase the velocity at which we build and ship analytics products by enforcing and shaping standards, developing analytics AI skills and context, and evolving team structures, in partnership with our Data Engineering, BI Engineering, and Product teams

• Lead the solution analytics leads as their manager, owning how the analytics team works day to day, scoping and sequencing work across solutions, and keeping people unblocked and focused

• Partner with our Data Platform Manager and Data Context & Semantic Architect to shape the BI platform and semantic architecture that supports both our standard embedded analytics products and the move toward self-service analytics (incl. Analytics agents)

• Stay hands-on, contributing directly as an IC in a domain when the work demands it, to unblock the team and to keep close to the craft you're holding others to

What We're Looking For:

• Demonstrated program ownership of a technical function: you have scoped, sequenced, and shipped analytics or data work across multiple parallel workstreams and held ultimate responsibility for quality and coherence, not just your own output

• Strong analytical rigor: you can take an ambiguous question to a precise, defensible answer, with the hands-on depth (SQL/dbt, modern warehouse and BI) to do the work yourself and set the standard, not just review against it

• A systems-builder instinct: you turn what works into repeatable process, standards, and enforcement that keep running without you, rather than holding the function together through personal effort

• Cross-functional influence across teams you don't directly control, with a track record of driving alignment when interpretations differ and holding durable working relationships with platform, engineering, and architecture partners

• Comfort with ambiguity and scale: you can take a coherent way of working that you've proven and re-establish it at broader scale across solutions and teams

It's a Plus if You Have…

• Expertise in the healthcare domain and familiarity with healthcare operational data, clinical workflows, hospital operations, or common healthcare measurement challenges

• Experience scaling an analytics function at a growing company, taking something that worked at smaller scale and rebuilding it as a system others can run

• Familiarity with data governance, metric governance, or semantic layer concepts, especially where consistency across teams, solutions, or customer implementations is critical

• Experience with data logic implemented in dbt and data visualization in Sigma, and with knowledge management systems for documenting metric definitions and analytical decisions

• Exposure to AI-enabled analytics, natural language analytics, or agentic analytics workflows, especially where high-quality metric definitions and trusted analytical context are required for safe and useful AI outputs

Compensation for this role is based on market data and takes into account a variety of factors, including location, skills, qualifications, and prior relevant experience. Salary is just one part of the total rewards package at Qventus. We also offer a range of benefits and perks, including Open Paid Time Off, paid parental leave, professional development, wellness and technology stipends, a generous employee referral bonus, and employee stock option awards.

jobs.title: Intern – Laboratory Testing Support
jobs.description:
ON.energy is setting the standard for large load interconnection. ON’s patented AI UPS™ is a medium-voltage UPS that serves as a firewall, protecting the data center from the grid, and the grid from the data center. With multiple gigawatts currently under construction, we are enabling grid-safe data centers.

ROLE SUMMARY

This is a six-month internship with structured assignments and increasing ownership. Strong performers may be considered for future full-time opportunities based on business need and role availability.  This Intern will support test planning and reporting product and system testing at the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) and ON.energy’s Houston laboratory. The intern will help turn engineering requirements into practical test plans, organize execution evidence, prepare clear draft reports by giving support to the laboratory engineers. This is a variable-term, remote R&D internship with optional travel.

Please Note: This is a remote position. Optional travel may include visits to NLR, Houston, or other test locations. On-site participation is subject to applicable access, training, and safety requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Test Plans: Help develop test plans and procedures that define the objective, required software/hardware setup and acceptance criteria. Maintain clear links between requirements, test activities, and results.

• Readiness: Support test readiness and daily planning by tracking key resources, dependencies, and open items.

• Execution Records: Maintain clear test logs and organize the supporting data, observations, and evidence for each test.

• Coordination: Keep plans and status information current across R&D, Commissioning Engineering, and external consultants. Follow up on missing inputs and review actions with the responsible technical leads.

• Issues: Document deviations and open questions for engineering review. Support test plan revisions and retest planning when needed.

• Data Analysis Tool: Build a reusable tool that can ingest lab test data in different formats and produce consistent, report-ready graphs. Document the tool so future data sets can be processed efficiently and results can be reproduced.

• Data Review: Check data quality, create plots, interpret and compare measured results with defined criteria under engineering direction.

• Reporting: Draft test reports and concise campaign summaries covering results, issues, and next steps. Clearly distinguish measured facts from interpretation and open questions.

• Document Control: Maintain organized revisions and source evidence in designated ON.energy repositories.

• Process Improvement: Help improve reusable templates and workflows for test planning, evidence management, and reporting.

KEY REQUIREMENTS

• Education: Currently pursuing or recently completed a B.S. or M.S. in electrical engineering, data science, or a related technical field.

• Technical Background: Coursework or project experience related to power systems, energy storage, power electronics or laboratory testing is preferred.

• Tools: Working knowledge of Excel and experience with Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or a similar data-analysis tool.

• Core Skills: Strong technical writing, attention to detail, and the ability to organize engineering information across a distributed team.

• Safety and Confidentiality: Follow laboratory safety, access, and confidentiality requirements. The intern will not perform energized electrical work unless a separately qualified and authorized user is present.

jobs.description:
Company Overview:

Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.  Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients.

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock.

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

This is an onsite position. Blink Health has offices in New York City (Flatiron District), St. Louis (Chesterfield), Pittsburgh (Robinson Twp.) and Seattle (Kirkland).

ABOUT THE ROLE

Blink Health is looking for a Senior Program Manager, People Operations to own our Leave of Absence and Accommodations programs end-to-end, while bringing deep People Ops expertise across a broader set of operational workstreams. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who thrives in building and running programs at scale — not just executing process, but designing the infrastructure behind it.

You will serve as the subject matter expert on all things LOA and ADA at Blink, partnering closely with HRBPs, legal counsel, managers, and employees to ensure every case is handled with care, consistency, and compliance. Beyond LOA and ADA, you'll flex into other People Ops workstreams — payroll, compliance, systems, onboarding/offboarding — as business needs demand.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Leave of Absence Program

• Serve as the primary point of contact for all leave of absence requests across federal, state, and local leave laws (FMLA, CFRA, PDL, PFL, ADA, company leave policies, and beyond)

• Work with our leave vendor, Sparrow to manage the full leave lifecycle — intake, eligibility determination, coordination with Sparrow (our leave platform), employee and manager communication, and return-to-work planning

• Maintain and continuously improve leave administration processes, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and a high-quality employee experience throughout

• Monitor evolving state and federal leave legislation and update policies and procedures accordingly

• Partner with Payroll to ensure accurate pay continuation, benefits deductions, and coordination during leave periods

Accommodations (ADA / PWFA)

• Own the end-to-end accommodations process in partnership with Disclo, our accommodations platform — from intake through resolution

• Conduct interactive process discussions with employees and managers; assess reasonable accommodations in alignment with regulatory and best practice accommodation standards

• Maintain thorough, confidential documentation for every accommodation case; partner with legal counsel as needed on complex situations

• Train managers on their role in the accommodations process and build their confidence in navigating sensitive conversations

People Ops Infrastructure & Flex Support

• Flex into broader People Ops workstreams — payroll, compliance, HRIS (Workday), onboarding/offboarding, and policy administration — as business needs require

• Identify gaps in existing processes and build scalable solutions; translate recurring problems into documented frameworks and systems

• Contribute to People Ops projects and initiatives across the team, bringing operational rigor and cross-functional coordination

• Support audits, reporting, and compliance workstreams including data integrity in Workday

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• 7+ years of People Operations experience, with at least 3–4 years of dedicated ownership over LOA and/or accommodations programs

• Deep working knowledge of federal and multi-state leave laws (FMLA, ADA, PWFA, CFRA, PDL, PFL, and equivalent state programs)

• Experience managing a high volume of leave and accommodation cases with precision, empathy, and sound judgment

• Strong Workday HCM experience — comfortable navigating absence management modules, reporting, and employee data

• A builder's instinct: you don't just follow process, you question whether the process is right and improve it when it isn't

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to translate complex compliance requirements into plain language for employees and managers

• High degree of discretion and comfort handling sensitive, confidential employee information

• Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple workstreams without losing the details

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience with Sparrow or another leave management platform

• Experience with Disclo or a similar accommodations platform

• Familiarity with payroll administration and how leave intersects with pay continuity

• Experience in a high-growth technology or healthcare company

Why Join Us:

It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year.  Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
