jobs.title: Recruitment Marketing Specialist
jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Learning and Development Specialist (Learning Content and OJT) is responsible for designing, implementing, and evaluating learning programs and initiatives to foster employee development and enhance organizational performance that are specific to the position. This position partners closely with production leaders and department managers to ensure employees receive the training, resources, and support needed to perform successfully and safely in their roles.
The position will not only develop training content but will also be analytical, detail-oriented, and eager to learn new skills. This position monitors program effectiveness through both qualitative and quantitative measures, including training records, competency attainment, KPI alignment, employee interactions, and feedback from department managers throughout the organization.
The ideal candidate is a self-starter who enjoys working with people, is highly organized and detail-oriented, and is comfortable balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic manufacturing environment. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, a proactive approach to problem-solving, and the ability to work effectively with employees at all levels of the organization.
 
COMPANY OVERVIEW
Component Repair Technologies, Inc. (CRT) began as a locally family-owned business, with operations in Mentor, OH since 1985, and grew into a global leader (500+ employees) in the aerospace MRO sector.  Specializing in the repair and overhaul of turbine engine components, CRT proudly serves the world’s largest airlines and jet engine manufacturers. Component Repair Technologies is focused on our valued employees, customers, and community. 
In 2025, CRT became a Safran Aircraft Engines company as a Center of Excellence for the repair of large jet engine parts in the Americas.
For over 120 years, Safran, through its Aircraft Engines subsidiary, designs, produces, markets and supports, alone or in partnership, aircraft engines offering world-class performance and reliability. Its core purpose is to contribute to a safer, more sustainable world, where air transport is more environmentally friendly, comfortable and accessible.
Operating through CFM International, its 50/50 joint venture with GE Aerospace, Safran Aircraft Engines is the world’s leading supplier of single-aisle commercial jet engines, the CFM56 and LEAP. Safran Aircraft Engines is fully committed to sustainable aviation through the RISE (Revolutionary Innovation for Sustainable Engines) technology development program. Safran Aircraft Engines also deploys a global network providing a full range of support, maintenance & repair services. 
Visit www.componentrepair.com and www.safran-group.com for more information. Take-off in your career, learn new skills and become part of a world-class workforce.
 
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follow established safety protocols and guidelines to ensure full compliance with company safety policies and procedures.
Design and deliver training programs (onboarding, on-the-job, leadership development, and technical skills) based on organizational objectives.
Design, develop, and deliver training programs that support employee development, operational effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and organizational objectives, including onboarding, on-the-job training (OJT), leadership development, technical skills, and professional development initiatives.
Create, update, and maintain training materials, job aids, educational resources, presentations, and course content for instructor-led, hands-on, and computer-based learning environments.
Partner with department managers and supervisors to identify training needs and develop structured training plans that support departmental goals and are aligned with the specific department and position.
Conduct training needs assessments and skills gap analyses to identify opportunities for workforce development and performance improvement.
Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs through feedback, surveys, and other assessment tools and make recommendations for curriculum improvement.
Maintain training records and ensure compliance with company, customer, regulatory, and audit requirements, including FAA Part 145 and other applicable industry standards.
Monitor industry trends and best practices in learning and development to enhance organizational learning initiatives.
Support employee development, career progression, and succession planning initiatives by providing guidance, resources, and visibility to internal development opportunities.
Administer and maintain the Learning Management System (LMS), ensuring accurate tracking of training compliance, employee development, and training-related data.
 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Learning and Development, Human Resources, Organizational Management, or a related field; or a minimum of two years of experience in a related role within a manufacturing or production environment.
Two to three years of experience in designing, implementing, and evaluating training and professional development programs for young adults and adult learners or relevant experience in a training or educational environment.
Demonstrated experience administering and maintaining a Learning Management System (LMS).
Demonstrated strength and experience in project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively and efficiently.
 
OTHER QUALIFICATIONS
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate with many different stakeholders. 
Previous experience as a mentor, coach, instructor, or trainer.
Excellent problem-solving abilities.
Ability to read, write, speak, understand English, and be able to effectively communicate with other employees.
Proficiency with software programs commonly used in training and development, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Learning Management Systems (LMS), and content authoring tools such as Articulate or similar platforms.
Experience in technical writing and editing documents that support employee training and production operations.
 
 WORK ENVIRONMENT
Safety Sensitive Environment: the successful candidate will be required to follow general shop safety procedures including the occasional use of safety glasses, safety toe shoes, and hearing protection.
Work standing and/or sitting during a normal shift. 
May be required to occasionally lift or move up to 10 pounds.
 
COMPANY BENEFITS
At CRT, our employees and their families are our most valued asset. We offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package that includes:
CRT currently offers two excellent health care options, one being a fully funded program (no premiums for employee and family) and the other being a traditional employee premium contribution.  Programs include health, vision, and dental coverages. Additional programs include short- and long-term disability and life insurance.
The company offers a 401k program with company match.
Continuing education is offered via multiple sources and opportunities with tuition reimbursement based on eligibility requirements.
Traditional paid time off (PTO) is offered via vacation days and personal days.
Multiple shift opportunities with hourly premiums for off-shifts are offered.
To review other benefits, visit our website at www.componentrepair.com/careers or Facebook page www.facebook.com/ComponentRepair  to see, “what we are up to.”
  
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER AND AFFIRMATIVE ACTION PARTICIPATION
Component Repair Technologies, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer, M/F/H/V.
CRT is committed to providing a safe and healthy workplace and promoting the health and well-being of its employees. It is the Company’s policy to only hire individuals who do not use drugs. All candidates will be screened for drug use prior to hire. Employment opportunities at CRT are open to all qualified applicants solely based on their job-related experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. CRT complies with all applicable federal, state and local laws with regard to equal employment opportunity.

jobs.title: Deployment & Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.

Position Overview

The Deployment & Support Engineer will be responsible for the successful installation, commissioning, and deployment of robotic systems at customer sites. This role ensures robots are installed, configured, tested, and operating according to technical and customer requirements.

When not actively performing deployments, the Deployment & Support Engineer provides customer and technical support for deployed robotic systems. This includes troubleshooting system issues, assisting customers with operational questions, coordinating issue resolution, and working closely with internal engineering and technical teams to maintain system performance and customer satisfaction.

The ideal candidate is technically capable, customer-focused, adaptable, and comfortable working in both field and remote environments.

Responsibilities

• Robot Deployment & Installation Lead and execute new robotic system deployments at customer sites. Prepare for deployments by reviewing site requirements, technical documentation, and project plans. Install, configure, and commission robotic systems and associated equipment. Perform system testing, validation, and troubleshooting to ensure successful operation. Coordinate with customers and internal teams to ensure deployment readiness. Train customer personnel on basic system operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting. Document deployment activities, system configurations, and outstanding issues. Ensure deployments are completed safely, efficiently, and according to established procedures. Identify and communicate technical risks, project delays, and deployment challenges. Customer & Technical Support Provide timely customer support for deployed robotic systems remotely Troubleshoot robot hardware, software, networking, and system integration issues. Assist customers with system operation, configuration, and technical questions. Diagnose issues, identify root causes, and implement or coordinate corrective actions. Monitor and follow up on customer-reported issues through resolution. Escalate complex or unresolved technical issues to the appropriate engineering or development teams. Support system upgrades, maintenance activities, and technical improvements. Maintain accurate records of support cases, troubleshooting steps, and resolutions. Help develop and maintain troubleshooting guides, support documentation, and standard operating procedures. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams to resolve technical issues. Provide feedback from customer sites to improve robot performance, reliability, and usability. Assist with testing new features, software releases, and hardware improvements. Contribute to the development of deployment and support processes. Share technical knowledge and best practices with team members. Support other deployment engineers and technical staff as needed.

Required Qualifications

• Experience in robotics, automation, mechatronics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer engineering, or a related technical field.

• Hands-on experience with the installation, troubleshooting, or maintenance of complex technical systems.

• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

• Ability to read and interpret technical documentation, wiring diagrams, and system specifications.

• Familiarity with computers, networking, software configuration, and technical troubleshooting.

• Strong communication and customer service skills.

• Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.

jobs.title: Superintendent, Los Angeles
jobs.description:
About Us: 

Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home. 

We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online. Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Come build your future with us.

Role Overview:

Homebound is seeking an experienced Construction Superintendent to join our Los Angeles team and lead field operations for our single-family home projects. As a Superintendent, you’ll be responsible for managing the entire construction process - from mobilization to delivery - with an uncompromising focus on safety and quality. Delivering homes on schedule and on budget is important, but secondary to building exceptional homes, safely.

This is an opportunity to help drive our Los Angeles wildfire rebuild efforts and provide essential housing solutions to support the community's recovery from the Altadena and Palisades fires earlier this year.

Homebound has a proven track record of successfully helping to rebuild communities after natural disasters, having supported recovery efforts in six disaster affected markets to date including; Fort Myers, FL, Santa Rosa, CA, and the Bahamas. We hope to bring that experience to Los Angeles to help rebuild lives and homes in the wake of these devastating wildfires.



What You'll Do:

 - Oversee and coordinate all aspects of on-site construction for your assigned homes.

 - Manage the simultaneous construction of up to 15 single-family homes in various stages.
   Monitor workmanship and adherence to scopes of work through checklists and field inspections.

 - Execute daily operations using Homebound’s proprietary project management software.

 - Approve trade partner work and associated invoices based on quality and completeness.

 - Lead on-site implementation of safety protocols and ensure compliance with local/national codes and permitting authority requirements.

 - Maintain both digital and physical project documentation.
   Proactively initiate and communicate changes to scope, plans, and specifications.

 - Follow established operational procedures for communication, change orders, and financial tracking.

 - Keep daily logs of site activity and coordinate inspections to maintain schedule momentum.
   Collaborate closely with Project Managers to support buyouts and provide feedback on budgeting and trade performance.

 - Participate in client walks and obtain occupancy permits upon completion.

 - Perform other construction-related duties as needed.

What You'll Bring:

 - 4+ years of experience in the construction industry (e.g., custom, infill, production), specifically with direct field experience in home building.

 - Proficient in reading and interpreting structural plans and blueprints independently.

 - Understanding of local building codes, permits, and the home construction process.

 - Experience working with project managers and trade partners to ensure projects stay on schedule and within budget.

 - Strong working knowledge of Excel for managing project schedules, budgets, and progress tracking.

 - A valid driver’s license.

 - Construction Certification (OSHA, LEAD, etc.) preferred



Our Commitment:

We are focused on building a diverse and inclusive workforce. If you’re excited about this role, but do not meet 100% of the qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply. To apply, please submit an application with your resume on the Career’s page. 

Homebound is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics or any other basis forbidden under federal, state, or local law. Homebound considers all qualified applicants in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.



Our Compensation Philosophy:

Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Please note that the salary range displayed on each job posting may vary by state. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter will share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Please note that each job posting includes a general description of any other compensation offered for the position in addition to the salary range displayed on the job posting. jobs.title: Senior Systems Engineer, Charging Systems
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Position Overview:

At Lucid, charging is not just a feature - it is a defining product attribute that blends high-voltage technology, system architecture, and customer experience into a seamless, industry-leading vehicle capability.

We are currently seeking Senior Systems Engineer, Charging Systems, to be part of a passionate, highly driven multi-disciplinary engineering team developing next-generation high-voltage(HV) systems and architectures. The successful candidate will exhibit a clear understanding of electric vehicle charging system and development thereof. The candidate will be responsible for definition of Model Based Systems Engineering deliverables of one or more charging features of Lucid products. This role will contribute to world-class charging attributes (e.g., fast charge rates, efficiency, battery health optimization) that directly impact range, cost, and customer experience.

The role will require cross-functional engagement with product management, vehicle engineering teams, software engineers, hardware engineers and verification and validation teams. A thorough understanding of system development lifecycle(s) is required to be successful in this role, gained through prior OEM or Tier 1 industry experience.

Our ideal candidate exhibits a proactive, can-do attitude and approaches their work systematically with vigor, determination and accuracy. Candidates will be expected to demonstrate excellence in their respective fields, to possess the ability to learn quickly and to strive for perfection within a fast-paced environment.

What you will do:

• Lead the end-to-end capture and definition of requirements for advancing leading class vehicle charging features, collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to shape cutting-edge EV experiences.

• Shape charging system architectures using Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), driving functional decomposition, signal definition, and cross-domain integration across vehicle systems.

• Translate high-level feature concepts into robust, implementable subsystem and component-level requirements that enable precise vehicle functionality

• Partner with Functional Safety Engineers to develop safety concepts, taking ownership of Technical Safety Concepts using proven methodologies such as FMEA and FTA

• Drive alignment with verification & validation teams to define comprehensive test strategies and ensure successful execution against requirements

• Collaborate closely with HV domain and software engineering teams to define, refine, and manage performance requirements for high-voltage system controls

• Contribute to the development and execution of product-level validation plans, ensuring features meet performance, safety, and customer expectations

• Investigate and resolve real-world vehicle charging issues through data-driven analysis, continuously enhancing system performance and user experience

• Coordinate systems engineering lifecycle activities with program management to successfully deliver milestones and product releases on schedule

• Champion continuous improvement of systems engineering practices, driving innovation and excellence across the organization

What you bring:

• 4+ years of experience delivering systems engineering solutions for automotive controls products in a production environment

• 4+ years of hands-on application of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) to drive design, analysis, and development workflows

• Deep working knowledge of vehicle charging standards, including SAE J1772/J3400 and ISO 15118

• Experience with Automotive embedded electronic product development

• Solid experience applying ISO 26262 to drive system requirements, architecture, and safety-driven design decisions

• Demonstrated ability to manage and deliver across multiple vehicle programs simultaneously in a fast-paced environment

• Strong data-driven problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyze and debug complex vehicle issues

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, able to convey complex technical concepts to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders

• Highly detail-oriented with a disciplined approach to documentation, traceability, and reporting

• Self-driven with a strong sense of ownership, a proactive mindset, and a collaborative approach to problem solving

Ways to Standout:

• Hands-on expertise with Cameo/Magic Cyber Systems Engineer and strong proficiency in SysML-based modeling

• Proven experience applying FMEA and structured risk management methodologies in complex engineering environments

• Solid understanding of electrical, electronic, and programmable systems, with the ability to connect system behavior to component-level design

• Familiarity with AUTOSAR architecture and its application in modern automotive software platforms

• INCOSE Systems Engineering certification (ASEP or CSEP), demonstrating a strong foundation in industry best practices

Education Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering or another related technical discipline is required.

• Master’s degree or higher education is preferred.

Salary Range: The compensation range for this position is specific to the locations listed below and is the range Lucid reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including job-related knowledge; skillset; experience, education and training; certifications; and other relevant business and organizational factors.

Base Pay Range (Annual)

$158,400—$217,800 USD

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Incentive and equity awards, if applicable, are determined based on individual performance, role scope, market considerations, and overall company results, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

Equal Opportunity: At Lucid, we believe diversity strengthens everything we build. Lucid Motors is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing an inclusive workplace for all. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable state or federal laws and regulations.

Accessibility: Lucid Motors is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need any accommodation to participate in the application process, please contact us at TA-Operations <@> lucidmotors.com. This email address is designated solely for accommodation requests and is not monitored for job applications or resume submissions. To be considered for employment, all applications must be submitted through the Lucid Motors Careers website.

Candidate Data Privacy: By submitting your application, you understand and agree that your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice.

To all recruitment agencies: Lucid Motors does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Lucid Motors. Lucid Motors is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.title: Order to Cash Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT WORKWHILE

WorkWhile is an AI-native labor platform serving enterprise customers across logistics, food production, retail, hospitality, events, and managed services. WorkWhile identifies the best hourly workers and matches them with shifts that fit their skills, location, and life. Businesses get access to a quality workforce, while workers get stable income and unmatched benefits, including next day pay, free telehealth services, and financial services.

We have the audacious goal to align incentives and solve inefficiencies in the labor market, disrupting the $650 billion staffing and recruiting market. Backed by Khosla Ventures and recognized by the Inc. 5000 for 10x growth, WorkWhile is reshaping the future of work.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Our customer mix has scaled faster than our finance and revenue operations, and we are hiring an Order-to-Cash Lead to take ownership of the full O2C function - strategy, execution, AI-powered automation and tooling.

 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN


STRATEGY & POLICY

 - Own the end-to-end Order to Cash process with a growth mindset. Proactively identify gaps, generate creative solutions, and roll up your sleeves to fix issues while thinking strategically about long-term process health and scalability.

 - Maintain standard invoicing and payments term framework. Review non-standard requests in incoming contracts and partner with Sales on a defined exception path

 - Regularly optimize credit policy: decisions on which customers go on invoicing vs. pay-by-bank/credit card, credit-limit setting, and the hold policy

 - Partner with the CFO on the cash-flow and financing implications of AR aging, including the company’s line of credit, borrowing base, and DSO trajectory


OPERATIONS & EXECUTION

 - Manage WorkWhile’s outsourced AR and collections team - set the operating cadence, metrics, and customer prioritization

 - Drive the open backlog; partner with AEs and AMs on aged AR; bring customer-specific issues to resolution

 - Enforce customer holds when warranted. Run the weekly AR/AM/Finance process and AR Analysis where holds are decided

 - Own VMS customer invoice reconciliation end-to-end. Partner with Operations on root-cause resolution, manage credit and payment allocation reconciliation, ensure WorkWhile invoice / customer VMS invoice / QBO financials tie out, and drive Engineering to build automation and API connections between systems.

 - Represent Finance externally on new customer invoice requirements and requests; own customer escalations on disputes and issues.

 - Serve as Finance Admin for WorkWhile internal Admin Portal for policy configurations that impact Customer Invoicing


PRODUCT & ROADMAP

 - Leverage modern AI-native tools to automate the O2C process - invoicing, cash application, dunning, reconciliation.

 - Enhance credit decisioning - replace today's manual spreadsheet workflow with a system-driven process for credit checks, payment-method routing, and credit-limit monitoring.

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, and Operations to build the invoicing path for VMS customers, including rate/hour/worker/shift reconciliation and hold-enforcement tooling.

 


WHO YOU ARE



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years in AR, billing, collections, credit, or O2C — with hands-on AND strategic experience. You can run a customer escalation and design a policy in the same week.

 - Track record of standing up or significantly improving credit and hold policies, including the cross-functional negotiation with Sales/AM that comes with it.

 - Comfortable managing an outsourced AR/collections team or BPO — setting KPIs, holding them accountable, and escalating issues effectively.

 - Familiarity with VMS/MSP customer chains or comparable third-party-payer environments, and with PO-driven billing workflows.

 - Direct experience partnering with Product/Engineering to scope and ship finance tooling — not just opening tickets.

 - Strong analytical fluency: QBO / NetSuite, AR dashboards, DSO and bad-debt KPIs, borrowing-base reporting.

 - Operates well in a high-growth, high-ambiguity environment. Marketplace, staffing, or labor-platform

 


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary + equity in a high-growth, venture-backed company

 - Hybrid work culture with office in SF

 - In-person company off-sites

 - Medical, dental & vision coverage

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 401(k)

 - WFH stipend to support your home office setup

WorkWhile has a diverse, mission-driven, and supportive culture—we look for people who want to take ownership, are energized by ambiguity, and strive to make a lasting impact. If this resonates with you, we’d love to chat!

jobs.title: Domino's Pizza Maker: Columbia Falls, MT - 734 9th St. W. #6 - (7025)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

You got game? You got spring in your step? You want the best job in the world! And schedules that work with you, not against you? That's right, we live to beat the rush and make it possible to make, bake or take pizzas during the hungry hours of the day and night, part or full time. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, hanging with your friends, or whatever. Sound good? Even if you just need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

We are searching for qualified customer service reps with personality and people skills. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, drop us a line. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From customer service representative to management, General Manager to Manager Corporate Operations or Franchisee, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 16 years of age or older.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

Additional Information:

• Employee discount
• Flexible schedule

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 4".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.title: Domino's Assistant Manager: Columbia Falls, MT - 734 9th St. W. #6 - (7025)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning, and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. Then you go to work, and you make sure that everyone there is doing what they need to do, even your boss. You just do that because you've always done it. Well maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance - Domino's Pizza is hiring bosses - more specifically assistant managers. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills - judgment, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From assistant manager to general manager, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members, and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties for All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

Additional Information:

• Employee discount
• Flexible schedule

Must be 18 years or older

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Treasury Associate
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY; Sandy, UT
jobs.description:
The Company You’ll Join

Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.

For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page.

The Problems You'll Solve

At Carta, our employees set out on a mission to unlock the power of equity ownership for more people in more places. We believe that the problems we solve today unlock the opportunities of tomorrow. As a Treasury Associate, you’ll work to:

• Daily Payment Exceptions & Platform Operations: Support payment exceptions handling of transaction failures and provide timely support to cross-functional business and support teams to resolve payment and funding issues in real-time.

• High-Volume Payment Approval & Specialized Disbursements: Oversee the review and approval of daily outgoing payment batches and manage the end-to-end disbursement and daily reconciliation processes for specialized corporate or transactional bank accounts.

• Bank Portal Security & Compliance Controls: Mitigate platform and transaction risks by administering daily fraud controls and reviewing transaction exception items across primary banking portals, while coordinating timely responses to banking compliance and regulatory inquiries.

• Daily Bank Data & Limit Monitoring: Maintain master banking data records and perform daily tracking and analysis of credit limits to support credit risk management and underwriting activities.

• Monthly Banking Audits & Statement Administration: Own monthly bank statement collection, archiving, and transaction export processes across global corporate bank accounts, and conduct comprehensive monthly pricing audits and fee reviews to reconcile service charges and eliminate variances.

• Liquidity Transfers & Platform Expansion: Assist in corporate cash and liquidity management by executing recurring intercompany transfer setups, responding to external bank authorization requests, and configuring system variables to support the onboarding of new geographical markets or banking partners.

The Team You'll Work With

You’ll join the Treasury team, which plays a vital role in managing overall banking related activities and supporting corporate and customer money movement across Carta. As a Treasury Associate, you will act as a key partner to our internal business units, helping monitor, review, and reconcile payment transactions that flow through our banking networks every day.

In this role, you will collaborate cross-functionally with team members in Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and our global banking partners. Your day-to-day focus will center on resolving payment exceptions, administering critical banking portal access, and partnering on continuous process improvements to ensure a seamless, secure, and highly scalable money movement experience for our clients.

About You

We are looking for a detail-oriented, tech-forward, and highly responsible professional who meets the following criteria:

• Experienced in Banking & Treasury/Payment Operations: 3+ years of experience in a finance, accounting, or related role recommended, with 2+ years of dedicated experience specifically in Treasury operations, banking operations, or payment processing recommended.

• Technical Skillset & AI-Forward Mindset: Advanced user of core spreadsheet applications (Excel/Google Sheets) with baseline proficiency in data querying utilities (such as Looker or Metabase), and a strong passion for utilizing modern AI tools (such as Claude or Gemini) to automate manual tasks and drive process efficiencies.

• Expertise in Global Banking & Payment Systems: Proficient knowledge of banking services (ACH, wire, F/X transfers), reconciliations, payment rules, compliance and controls (such as NACHA guidelines, OFAC regulations, and bank portal administration).

• Autonomy & Project Ownership: A largely independent operator who is highly productive under general guidelines, exercises sound judgment to resolve moderate-scope operational issues using established procedures, and takes full ownership of low-complexity ad-hoc projects.

• Documentation & Detail Orientation: Rigorous attention to detail and an established record of executing tasks accurately and meeting tight deadlines, paired with a passion for creating and maintaining clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), reconciliations, and process flow mappings to eliminate single-source-of-knowledge risks.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication: A proactive collaborator who routinely partners within the treasury team and demonstrates emerging capabilities to work with Support, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Compliance, with the ability to clearly present analysis and communicate with business and technical stakeholders

At Carta, you’re not just an employee. You’re a builder who is creating  infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership. Cartans are helpful, relentless, unconventional and kind; representing Carta’s Identity Traits. They work collaboratively and cross functionally  to challenge the status quo; working towards a common goal of creating more owners in the private markets.

Salary

Carta’s compensation package includes a market competitive salary, equity for all full time roles, exceptional benefits, and, for applicable roles, commissions plans. Our minimum cash compensation range for this role is:
$93,500 - $120,000  in New York and San Francisco
$74,800 - $88,000  in Sandy, Utah

Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on geography, candidate experience and expertise, and other factors.

Disclosures:

• We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing a positive interview experience for every candidate. If accommodations due to a disability or medical condition are needed, please connect with the talent partner via email.

• Carta uses E-Verify in the United States for employment authorization. See the E-Verify and Department of Justice websites for more details.

• For information on our data privacy policies, see Privacy, CA Candidate Privacy, and Brazil Transparency Report.

• Please note that all official communications from us will come from an @carta.com or @carta-external.com domain. Report any contact from unapproved domains to security@carta.com.

jobs.title: Manager, Forecasting
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

Position Title: Manager, Forecasting

Department: Portfolio Strategy

Reports To: Director, Portfolio Strategy

Location: Evanston, IL – On-site 4 days per week (Mon to Thurs)

Job Overview

Kardigan is hiring a Manager, Forecasting to turn data into the insights that guide strategic and operational decisions across our portfolio. Sitting within the Portfolio Strategy team, you will own how patient / revenue forecasts get built, synthesized and communicated. This position will collaborate closely with Insights & Analytics teams to provide input on key data points to gather from primary and secondary market research across patients, physicians, and payers. The role partners broadly across the organization, including Portfolio Strategy, Corporate Strategy, Product Strategy, Commercial, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, R&D, Program Management and Business Development. Success here depends on analytical rigor: framing ambiguous questions, pressure-testing the underlying data, and reconciling signals that arrive from very different sources. The position also requires business acumen and a deep understanding of pharmaceutical operations to ensure the successful development, launch and growth of our products. The position is based in Evanston, IL.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Lead forecasting across the portfolio, building the projection models behind both active programs, indication expansions, and prospective candidates

• Partner with Finance and Portfolio Strategy to deliver forecasts for the long-range plan, annual operating plan and budget cycles, ensuring alignment of assumptions across functions

• Ad hoc forecasting and analytics in partnership with investor relations to inform board meetings, earnings calls, and investor discussions

• Support business development activities by forecasting revenue opportunities for prospective asset candidates

• Partner with competitive intelligence to evaluate competitor clinical results and anticipated market dynamics; translate key findings into impacts on internal forecasts

• Own forecast governance, including documentation of assumptions, version control, reconciliation of actuals versus forecast, and tracking and improving forecast accuracy over time

• Analyze secondary data, including patient claims and epidemiology studies, alongside market research findings to characterize patient populations, determine market segmentation and uncover trends

• Build and maintain patient-flow and scenario models, running sensitivity analyses against target product profiles, clinical outcomes and launch timing to quantify risk and upside for decision makers

• Track how pricing, payer behavior and coverage hurdles are shifting, and feed these inputs into pricing and market access strategy

• Provide demand and volume forecasts to support launch readiness, supply planning and manufacturing, and commercial resource decisions such as field force sizing

• Identify emerging trends and areas of unmet need within priority disease areas to inform portfolio prioritization

• Raise the standard for how analytics are completed, choosing the right data assets, vendors and methods for the question at hand and codifying what works

• Present and discuss forecasts, assumptions, insights and recommendations with internal stakeholders and senior leadership; mentor junior analysts as the function grows

Qualifications and Preferred Skills

• Bachelor’s degree required and a minimum of 5 years of consulting, investment, marketing, consulting, forecasting, or agency experience in healthcare/biopharmaceuticals. MBA or advanced degree preferred.

• Forecasting and Modeling: Proficiency in data analysis and financial modeling, including forecast, valuation and scenario models.

• Data and Market Research: Experience conducting and/or evaluating secondary data sources and primary market research, with the ability to interpret complex scientific and market data, identify key trends and extract meaningful insights.

• Collaboration: Ability to effectively collaborate across multiple functions and with internal and external stakeholders of various backgrounds and skill sets. Skilled in establishing a collaborative and respectful environment.

• Communication: Writes and presents with clarity, and can make a complex analysis land with scientists, commercial leaders, and executives alike.

• Industry Knowledge: Deep familiarity with the healthcare landscape — managed care and payers, patients, providers, biopharma companies, and the technologies and disease-area trends reshaping them.

• Strategic Thinking: Strong strategic thinking with the ability to synthesize market data, customer insights and scientific information into actionable recommendations.

• Business Excellence: Strong project and process management skills including the ability to manage multiple projects, set priorities and meet deadlines.

• Critical Thinking: Strong critical thinking and structured, problem-solving skills.

• Agility: Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, often ambiguous environment, and adapts as priorities shift.

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$142,000—$185,000 USD

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.
Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

Standing
Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Walking
For short distances for short durations
Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting
Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting
Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying
Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.
During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing walking and climbing duties.

Pushing
To move trays which are placed on dollies.
A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24 - 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing
Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.
During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Additional Job Details

ADDITIONAL JOB DETAILS

Stooping/Bending
Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting
Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching
Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
Workers reach above 72 occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving
Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks
Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.
Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids
Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties
Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.
Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.
Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. Then you go to work and you make sure that everyone there is doing what they need to do, even your boss. You just do that because you've always done it. Well maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance - Domino's Pizza is hiring bosses - more specifically general managers. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills - judgment, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance& punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the
phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTSincluding, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile"bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72"high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24"- 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72"occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing"walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Lead
jobs.description:
THE PROBLEM


Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.




Role in one line: Permanently own the definitions, system behavior, routing, forecast, and instrumentation behind Harper's revenue funnel.



Two dashboards disagree about the same funnel. A stage changed without the owner changing. The forecast moved, but nobody can trace why. Those are not reporting annoyances. They are failures in the operating system you own.



Harper is scaling an AI-native commercial insurance operation across three offices. Atlanta adds frontline volume. New York adds a second headquarters. This San Francisco role keeps one inspectable revenue system underneath all of it.




WHY NOW



Revenue Operations is the permanent owner of funnel definitions, customer relationship management system behavior, routing, forecasting, and revenue instrumentation. When another team proves a temporary fix, this role decides how it enters the permanent system, operates it, and keeps it reconciled.



This role does not own frontline sales management, customer conversations, placement strategy, marketing creative, or temporary cross-functional projects whose permanent home has not yet been decided.




WHAT YOU OWN



 - Own funnel definitions. Maintain the canonical meaning, entry rule, exit rule, source, and accountable owner for each revenue state.

 - Own CRM behavior. Define and maintain fields, validations, automations, permissions, and state transitions around the canonical funnel.

 - Own routing. Keep assignment logic, exceptions, ownership changes, and escalation paths inspectable and tested.

 - Own forecasting. Publish the forecast method, inputs, assumptions, version, and variance back to actual booked revenue.

 - Own revenue instrumentation. Make demand, contact, intake, quote, close, bind, and booked revenue reconcile to their source records.

 - Run funnel analysis. Find where volume, conversion, speed, or handoffs break and turn the finding into a specific operating action.

 - Protect routing and ownership. Make sure every live opportunity has the right owner, next action, and escalation path.

 - Partner with operators. Work in the sales, intake, placement, and service workflows before changing them.

 - Automate repeat work with controls. Use enrichment, generated notes, task creation, quality checks, and reporting only when the source, failure state, and human correction path remain visible.

 - Measure the change. Prove whether a workflow, campaign, routing decision, or sales motion changed conversion, speed, or revenue.




THE OPERATING PROOF



 - Funnel states have one canonical definition, source, entry rule, exit rule, and accountable owner.

 - Reported metrics reconcile to source records for the same population and window.

 - Live opportunities keep one current owner, one next action, and a recorded routing reason.

 - Routing changes carry a test case, approval owner, effective date, and rollback path.

 - Forecasts preserve their inputs, assumptions, version, and variance to actual booked revenue.

 - Automated writes expose their source, resulting state, failure state, and correction path.

 - Temporary fixes that belong in the revenue system reach a permanent owner, operating documentation, instrumentation, and a verified run.




WHO THRIVES HERE



 - You have owned revenue operations, sales operations, growth operations, or a comparable operating system in a fast-growing company.

 - You understand CRM architecture, lifecycle stages, routing, attribution, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene.

 - You can write SQL or work directly enough with data to test a claim yourself.

 - You move from analysis to operating change and then measure whether the change worked.

 - You can partner with sales leaders and frontline operators without turning every problem into a process meeting.

 - You have operated generated notes, enrichment, routing, task creation, or reporting automations with visible source data, failure states, and correction paths.

 - You care more about booked revenue and conversion than dashboard activity.

 - You are based in San Francisco or ready to relocate.




WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY



 - You want to administer a CRM without owning the revenue outcome.

 - You produce reports but do not make operating recommendations.

 - You want to own sales management, account placement, marketing creative, or every temporary cross-functional problem.

 - You rely on field completeness as proof that the underlying process works.

 - You need a remote or hybrid default.




LOCATION



 - Working location: San Francisco, on-site.




BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Commuter benefits

 - Team meals and snacks




THE PROCESS



 1. Founder screen — Initial fit and alignment

 2. On-site day — Meet the team, work through real scenarios




HOW TO APPLY



Send your resume and a short revenue-operations example. Describe one funnel or CRM problem that looked like a data issue but was really an operating issue, how you proved it, what you changed, and the revenue or conversion result.
